full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Abdur Rashid, J : The judgment-debtor Executive Engineer (Roads and Highways) Road Division at Shariatpur obtained the Rule upon making an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against an order dated 22.08.02 passed by the District Judge at Barisal in Money Execution Case No. 01 of 2002, which rejected an application for stay of further proceedings. 

 3. Then, on 30.01.02 the opposite party made an application before the Deputy Commissioner, Rangamati being Money Execution Case No. 07 of 2002 for realization of Tk. 41,82,166.00. The case was then sent to the court of District Judge at Barisal and Money Execution Case No. 01 of 02 was registered on 19.02.02. Pursuant to the notice, the petitioner appeared and on 05.06.02 filed a written objection to the award. Same date the petitioner made an application for stay of further proceeding of the execution case till disposal of the Title Suit No. 08 of 2002 which he instituted on 14.01.02 in the first court of Joint District Judge at Shariatpur. By the impugned order the application for stay was rejected. Hence, the Rule. 

 5. The opposite party opposed the Rule by filing an affidavit. In the affidavit, it is stated that Title Suit No. 08 of 2002 filed in the court of join District Judge at Shariatpur was misconceived and the learned Joint District Judge returned the plaint as he had no jurisdiction to entertain such suit. On 17.03.03 plaint of the suit was returned and the present rule was obtained on 09.07.03 suppressing those facts. 

 6. Mr. Joynal Abedin, learned Assistant Attorney General submits that the petitioner already filed written objection for setting aside the award, which is still pending before the execution court. Petitioner also instituted a suit for setting aside the award which is now pending before the Deputy Commissioner, Rangamati. He submits that if the execution case be allowed to proceed then the petitioner will suffer irreparable loss and injury. 

 7. Opposing the Rule, Mr. Tapan Chakraborty learned Advocate submits that by order dated 17.05.03 the plaint was returned by the joint District Judge on the view that the suit was beyond his jurisdiction. After return of the plaint, the petitioner again filed it before the Deputy Commissioner at Rangamati. In view of the Arbitration Act, 2001, no suit is maintainable to challenge any award given by an Arbitrator. The application for stay of further proceeding of the execution case pending disposal of such misconceived suit was nothing but a device to delay payment of the awarded money. 

 8. He submits that learned District Judge, Barisal did not commit any error in rejecting the prayer for stay of further proceeding of the execution case, which does not call for any interference. 

 11. On 30.01.02 opposite party made an application purportedly under section 44 of the Arbitrator Act. 2001 before the Deputy Commissioner at Rangamati for enforcement of the award and the application was registered as a Money Execution Case NO. 07 of 02 on a order sheet of a Magistrate. By order .dated 03.02.02 the case was however sent back to the District Judge at Barisal. But none of the orders was signed by the Deputy Commissioner at Rangamati or anybody. After receipt of the case, the learned District Judge at Barisal registered the case as Money Execution case No. 01 of 02. Pursuant to the notice, the petitioner appeared and on 29.05.02 filed a written objection for setting aside the award. 

 12. It also appears that the petitioner instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 08 of 02 in the first Court of Joint District Judge at Shariatpur. By order dated 17.05.03 plaint of the suit was returned by the learned District Judge on the view that . the suit was beyond his jurisdiction. Then, the petitioner filed the plaint again before the Deputy Commissioner, Rangamati. By order dated 17.1.1.03 plaint was accepted after hearing and the opposite party was asked to show fixing on 11.01.04 for return of service. The case was registered as Civil Suit no. 169 of 03. 

 13. Only issue facing us whether the learned District Judge committed any error resulting in any failure of justice by rejecting the prayer for stay of further proceeding of the execution case.
